descriptor: Japanese personal-care & chemicals conglomerate · FY ends 31 March · reported in JPY · segments restructured 2018, 2021 & 2023

charts.title: Gross Profit, Operating Income & Net Income

sections.title: Segment Mix
sections.subtitle: Kao restructured its reporting segments in 2018, 2021 and 2023; each bar shows whichever segment set was in force that year, so series start and stop rather than running the full history.

charts.title: Segment Revenue by Era
charts.annotation: Chemical is the one segment name Kao kept through every restructuring, so it is the only continuous bar; every other series is populated only for the years its segment name was in use.

charts.title: Segment Operating Profit by Era
charts.annotation: Cosmetics and Health & Beauty Care (2023 onward) absorbed the former Skin & Hair Care and Human Health Care lines, which is why profit per segment cannot be chained year over year across the 2023 cut.

charts.title: Net Income vs Free Cash Flow vs Owner FCF
charts.annotation: Owner FCF, where shown, is the DCF's series after SBC, interest income and lease principal.

segmentRevenue.title: Segment revenue by era
segmentRevenue.content:
Kao has restructured its reported business segments three times -- pre-2018 (Consumer Products / Beauty Care / Chemical), 2018-2022 (added Human Health Care, Skin & Hair Care, Fabric & Home Care, then folded most of these into Hygiene & Living Care and Life Care from FY2020), and FY2023 onward (Cosmetics, Health & Beauty Care, Hygiene & Living Care, Life Care, Sanitary Products, Business Connected, Chemical).

For Kao Corporation: each bar is only populated for the years its segment name was actually reported -- bars do not run continuously across the chart, by design, rather than being spliced into a false continuous series. Chemical is the one name Kao kept throughout.

What to watch:

  • Whether the newest structure (Cosmetics / Health & Beauty Care) is growing faster than the legacy skin/hair and human-health lines it replaced
  • Chemical's steady climb against the much larger but slower consumer segments
  • FY2023 is the first year of the latest structure, so only three years of comparable history exist for Cosmetics, Health & Beauty Care, Sanitary Products and Business Connected

segmentOperatingProfit.title: Segment operating profit by era
segmentOperatingProfit.content:
Operating profit for the same shifting segment set as the revenue chart above -- see that chart for the three reorganisation dates.

For Kao Corporation: margin pressure shows up here before it shows up in group operating margin, since the largest segment (Consumer Products, later Hygiene & Living Care) dilutes a smaller segment's swings. Human Health Care and Skin & Hair Care both had falling operating profit into FY2020, the years just before Kao merged them away.

What to watch:

  • Any segment whose profit falls while its revenue (chart above) holds up or rises -- cost or mix pressure
  • Chemical's operating profit relative to its revenue growth (margin trend) across all three eras, the one true like-for-like comparison available
  • Business Connected and Sanitary Products, the newest and smallest segments, only have two full years of profit history

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Kao Corporation: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Kao Corporation: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Kao Corporation: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Kao Corporation: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Kao Corporation: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Kao Corporation: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Kao Corporation: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Kao Corporation: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Kao Corporation: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Kao Corporation: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
